question: What term refers to the amount of alcohol present in a person's bloodstream?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,d:Driving under influence level (DUI level).
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood; higher BAC levels indicate greater impairment.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing and the train passes, you should:
options: a:Look for a second train and wait for signals to stop flashing.,b:Immediately proceed once the visible train passes.,c:Drive around crossing gates if they stay down briefly.,d:Honk to signal your intent to cross.
note: There may be another train on adjacent tracks; wait until all gates are up and signals stop before proceeding.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color background?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs (speed, stop, yield, etc.) are usually white rectangles or squares with colored symbols or text.

question: Work zone barrels, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Keep drivers out of hazardous work areas.,b:Inconvenience drivers intentionally.,c:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: These devices guide and protect drivers and workers by keeping traffic out of dangerous parts of the work zone.

question: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow line means:
options: a:You may pass from the side next to the broken line when it is safe.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: When the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross it to pass if it is safe; the solid line side may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive off the paved road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No — you may not drive off the main traveled portion of the road to pass.,b:Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Yes, if there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
note: Do not drive onto the shoulder to pass; passing must be done within the proper travel lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, you should:
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop in the intersection, and c:Increase your speed to avoid collisions.
note: If you are within the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear it safely rather than stopping in it.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe.,b:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposing lanes and mean that passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: In fog, rain, or snow you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare from reflected moisture and help you see better in precipitation and fog.

question: Why is driving at night generally more dangerous than driving in daylight?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,c:The road is always more slippery at night.,d:Oncoming headlights eliminate glare.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from oncoming lights mean you cannot see as far at night; use headlights and be cautious.

question: Because motorcycles and similar small vehicles can be hard to spot, you should:
options: a:Make constant visual checks and be especially alert.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,c:Slow down every time you see one.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots; check mirrors frequently and look carefully before changing lanes or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After you pass another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:After you have signaled for three seconds.,c:When the other driver signals you to return.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror, indicating enough space.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle will yield the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work is ahead.
note: Slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment or maintenance vehicles display an orange-red triangle on the back to warn other drivers.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting is best to use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you begin a turn but then decide not to, you should:
options: a:Complete the turn you started.,b:Signal and rejoin traffic by backing up.,c:Quickly steer back to the previous lane.,d:Stop in the intersection and wait.
note: Once committed to a turn, follow through; abrupt corrections can cause collisions.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is true?
options: a:Many cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b:Over-the-counter meds never impair driving if used as directed.,c:Prescribed medications are always safe to drive on.,d:Medications only affect drivers over 65.
note: Both prescription and OTC medications can impair driving; many cold/allergy meds cause drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Attempt to change lanes in an intersection.,b:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Signal your intended move.
note: Never change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: When vehicles are stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights, they must remain stopped until:
options: a:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted.
note: Motorists must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, and remain stopped until the lights are off, the arm is withdrawn, and the bus moves.

question: If you see a lane-control sign with an arrow and the word "ONLY" under it above your lane, you must:
options: a:Travel in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Always make a lane change.,c:Ignore it if traffic is light.
note: Lane-control signs require you to use the indicated lane movement (for example, left-only) as shown by the arrow and "ONLY".

question: A truck's "No zones" refer to areas where cars:
options: a:Disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck driver's ability to stop or maneuver.,b:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: No zones are the large blind areas around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be hidden or too close, increasing crash risk.

question: Whenever you park on any hill, you should:
options: a:Set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park" (or in gear).,b:Let the vehicle roll slightly and then set the parking brake.,c:Always point your front wheels straight ahead regardless of curb presence.
note: On hills you should leave the car in park or in gear and engage the parking brake; also turn wheels appropriately depending on curb.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic may not move in the arrow's direction.,b:You may turn in that direction after stopping.,c:You may turn in that direction with caution.,d:The direction has right-of-way.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits traffic from moving in that direction until a green signal appears.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle from the corner of your eye.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,d:Flash your high beams back at them.
note: Avoid looking directly at incoming high beams; focus on the right edge and use peripheral vision to track the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A green arrow signal requires you to:
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection, then turn in the arrow's direction.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians in the intersection.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:All of the above (alertness, concentration, reaction time, coordination).,b:Alertness and concentration only.,c:Reaction time and coordination only.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs reduce alertness, concentration, slow reaction time, and impair coordination.

question: When visibility is very poor due to fog, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use low-beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Use high-beam headlights.,d:Turn on only parking lights.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) because high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination sooner.,c:Turn up the radio and drive on.,d:Drink energy drinks and continue driving.
note: If you are too tired to drive safely, stop to rest or change drivers; naps are effective at restoring alertness.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and/or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed, yielding right-of-way.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection indicates:
options: a:You may proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if the way is clear.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green means you may go when the intersection is clear, yielding to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Stopping distances increase and crashes become more severe.,b:Stopping distances decrease as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and make collisions more severe, increasing risk of injury or death.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using siren and flashing lights, you must yield by:
options: a:Driving as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stopping.,b:Changing into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.,c:Stopping in the middle of an intersection immediately.
note: Move toward the right edge of the roadway and stop, taking care not to block intersections, until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a public road and you must stop, you should:
options: a:Pull off to the right side of the road, if possible, and turn on your hazard lights.,b:Stop in your lane and hold down the horn to attract attention.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle running.
note: When possible, get off the traveled portion of the road and use emergency flashers to show you need assistance.

question: If you continually pass vehicles on a two-lane road because you drive faster than others, what is most likely to happen?
options: a:It will get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Your chances of a collision will increase.,c:You will help prevent traffic congestion.,d:You will improve your fuel economy.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads raises your collision risk; avoid unnecessary passing when possible.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads you should:
options: a:Slow down because your tires have less traction than on pavement.,b:Drive at the same speed as on pavement because traction is unchanged.,c:Expect better visibility than on paved roads.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and lengthen stopping distance; reduce speed and drive cautiously on gravel or dirt roads.

question: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass, while those next to the solid line may not.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass at any time.,c:The side next to the solid line may pass.
note: When a broken line borders a solid yellow, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line when it is safe.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to warn drivers about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance conditions.,b:General warnings.,c:Regulatory requirements.
note: Orange signs specifically indicate construction or maintenance areas and alert drivers to changed conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than traffic.,c:The posted speed limit regardless of traffic speed.,d:Below 25 mph to safely merge.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the correct action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, steer straight, slow down gradually, and use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it.,c:Pull over quickly and brake hard.
note: If a blowout occurs, grip the wheel, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and slow gradually before pulling off the road in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a level roadway with no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail; on level roads leave wheels straight.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead into the headlights.
note: Look briefly toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining enough vision to stay on course.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Using high beams in fog.,c:Staring only at the road ahead.
note: To maintain awareness of hazards, scan the road and check mirrors every few seconds; do not stare only ahead.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Missing an exit only.,c:Being late for appointments.,d:Improved concentration.
note: Tiredness slows decisions and may lead to falling asleep, causing serious crashes.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, you should not:
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself by pressing against the seatback.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.,d:Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel.
note: Do not release your belt; brace against the seatback and head restraint to reduce whiplash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Slowing down just to look at a collision or unusual event:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow.,d:Is encouraged for safety reasons.
note: Rubbernecking slows traffic and contributes to congestion and secondary crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions and go through without stopping.,b:Stop and wait for the light to turn green.,c:Refuse and follow the signal light instead.,d:Call for confirmation from another officer.
note: Officer instructions supersede traffic signals; obey the officer's directions.

question: You should yield to a pedestrian:
options: a:At all times when necessary to prevent striking them, even if they are not obeying traffic laws.,b:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,c:Only if traffic lights favor the pedestrian.,d:Only when a crossing guard is present.
note: Always do what you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian regardless of who is breaking the law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and/or pavement markings permit passing and you have enough room to do so safely.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Only pass where pavement markings and signs allow it and you have adequate space and visibility to complete the maneuver safely.

question: When parking in an area not normally used for parking, you must:
options: a:Ensure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Leave your reverse lights on.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: Make sure your parked vehicle does not create a hazard; position it so approaching drivers can see it from all directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed limit and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to beat the light.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.
note: A steady yellow means prepare to stop; if you can stop safely before the intersection, do so; otherwise proceed cautiously.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road when possible.,b:Stop in your traffic lane and flash your hazard lights.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.
note: If possible, get your vehicle off the road away from traffic and turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers know you are stopped.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign.
note: Five-sided (pentagon) signs are used to warn drivers about school zones and school crossings where children may be present.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:Any amount of alcohol in your system.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Kentucky enforces zero tolerance for underage drivers; any detectable alcohol can lead to license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass another vehicle when:
options: a:There is a broken line next to your lane indicating passing is permitted.,b:You are on a hill or curve with limited visibility.,c:There is a solid line next to your lane prohibiting passing.
note: A broken line beside your lane indicates you may pass when it is safe; never pass where lines prohibit it or visibility is limited.

question: Approaching an octagonal sign you must:
options: a:Stop.,b:Slow.,c:Turn.
note: An octagon-shaped sign always means STOP; come to a full stop and yield to others with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving a parallel parking space alongside the road you should:
options: a:Signal your intent and look over your shoulder before moving.,b:Look only in your mirrors and then go.,c:Not use a turn signal to avoid confusing traffic.
note: Signal and check over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before reentering traffic from parallel parking.

question: Your chest should be approximately how far from the center of the steering column?
options: a:10 to 12 inches.,b:5 inches.,c:20 inches.
note: Adjust the seat so your chest is about 10–12 inches from the steering column and your shoulders are not below the top of the wheel.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first when temperatures drop?
options: a:A bridge.,b:An intersection.,c:A tunnel.
note: Bridges and overpasses often freeze before other road surfaces because they are exposed to cold air above and below the pavement.

question: In Kentucky, when can drivers of passenger vehicles legally use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals?
options: a:Never (passenger vehicles must use mechanical signals).,b:If the vehicle is not equipped with mechanical turn signals.,c:If the driver prefers to use hand signals.
note: Kentucky requires functioning mechanical turn signals on passenger vehicles; hand signals are not an allowed substitute for them (except for some farm, construction, animal-drawn vehicles, or bicycles).

question: When you spot pedestrians near the road, you should:
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give pedestrians space since they may enter your path unexpectedly.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and remain in your vehicle if possible.,b:Get out of the vehicle and flag down passing cars.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get attention.,d:Exit your vehicle onto the roadway to warn others.
note: Stop on the shoulder, use emergency flashers, and stay in the vehicle if it’s safe to do so because of high-speed traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Slow and drive through if clear.,d:Ignore it and proceed as normal.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, then proceed when safe.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off children, drivers must:
options: a:Stop regardless of the direction you are traveling.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop only if children are present.
note: When a school bus is stopped and displaying its stop signal, drivers in both directions must stop until the children are safe and signals are retracted.

question: Is it advisable to always drive more slowly than surrounding traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be hazardous.,b:Yes — always drive slower as a defensive technique.,c:Yes — driving more slowly is always safer than faster driving.
note: While you should slow down in poor conditions, driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can cause congestion and increase crash risk.

question: In foggy conditions, what lighting choice improves safety?
options: a:Use high beam headlights.,b:Use parking lights only.,c:Use low beam headlights.,d:Turn on four-way flashers.
note: Low-beam headlights are recommended in fog, rain, or snow since high beams can worsen visibility by reflecting off the moisture.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:Near blind pedestrians.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.,d:To warn another driver of danger.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; it may startle and create danger. Yield and wait.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Yield only to vehicles on the left.
note: A flashing yellow warns drivers to proceed with caution and be alert for cross traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often, whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Never; always insist on it.,c:Only at marked intersections.,d:Only when directed by an officer.
note: Never assume others will yield; give up your legal right-of-way when doing so prevents a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into:
options: a:The first available lane on the one-way street.,b:Any lane you choose.,c:The second lane on the one-way street.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, make the turn from the lane closest to the direction you are going into the first legal lane on the one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a left-turn lane and there is oncoming traffic, you should:
options: a:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your front wheels straight until turning.,b:Turn your front wheels left in preparation to turn.,c:Move left of the center lane to make space for the turn.
note: Signal in advance and keep the wheels straight to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind; begin the turn when safe.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:To alert inattentive drivers by vibration and sound when leaving the travel lane.,b:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.,d:To reduce vehicle speed by roughening the road.
note: Rumble strips create sound and vibration to warn drivers they are straying from the lane or approaching hazards.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in your mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are regions near the rear corners of your vehicle not visible in mirrors; always check them by glancing over your shoulder when changing lanes.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic light means you may:
options: a:Not turn in the arrow's direction until the light changes.,b:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn after coming to a full stop.,d:Turn if the intersection is clear.
note: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for a green signal or arrow before turning.

question: Before changing lanes you should check mirrors and also:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Always slow down significantly.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.,d:Signal only after starting to move.
note: Look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes in addition to mirror checks.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More coordinated.,b:More sober.,c:More intoxicated.,d:Less likely to be detected.
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood; higher BAC produces greater impairment.

question: If you drive more slowly than the normal flow of traffic, what is the most likely outcome?
options: a:You will interfere with traffic and may receive a ticket.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,d:You will be rewarded by police.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can block normal movement and may lead to a citation; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
options: a:In a marked or unmarked crosswalk or otherwise crossing the street.,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only crossing a specific lane.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk and, for safety, should yield to anyone crossing the street.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn them.,b:Start to prepare to slow down only.,c:Flash your headlights.,d:Swerve around them immediately.
note: When a pedestrian—especially a child—is about to enter your path, a sharp horn blast can warn and prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on state highways is:
options: a:55 mph.,b:65 mph.,c:75 mph.
note: Unless a different limit is posted, the default speed limit on state highways is 55 miles per hour.

question: Changing lanes from one lane to another is best done:
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Make lane changes slowly and deliberately, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots to avoid collisions.

question: A driver's license should be considered a:
options: a:Privilege, not a right.,b:Right, not a privilege.,c:Requirement.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state; it must be earned and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: Kentucky law prohibits operating a motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher for drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When, if ever, may you drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.,d:When signs permit it.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; other drivers won't expect you there and it creates a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return safely to the drive lane.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Maintain speed and position regardless of danger.
note: Give the passing vehicle room to re-enter the lane as soon as it is safe so you both can avoid approaching hazards.

question: When driving in fog or mist you should avoid using high beam headlights because:
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you as well.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog and mist back toward the driver, decreasing visibility and making it harder to see the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin reducing speed as you prepare to exit the interstate?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.,d:Only after the exit ramp ends.
note: Maintain freeway speed until you reach the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the exit advisory speed.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck, you should be prepared to:
options: a:Stop at all railroad crossings.,b:Pass them on the right.,c:Expect them to exceed the speed limit.,d:Signal them to move faster.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings; be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street you should position your vehicle:
options: a:Near the centerline (in the lane closest to the center).,b:Near the right-hand side of the road.,c:To the left of the centerline.
note: Begin your left turn from the lane closest to the centerline, and turn into the first legal lane on the destination road.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment.,b:Vision.,c:Balance.,d:Hearing.
note: Judgment is typically the first mental function impaired by alcohol, affecting decision-making and risk assessment.

question: Excessive speed often:
options: a:Leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash likelihood.,b:Increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:Does not change crash risk.
note: Driving too fast is a leading factor in crashes and often causes risky choices and reduced time to react to hazards.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,b:They generally affect only large vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility issues.,d:They are only a hazard to cyclists.
note: Strong wind can move or destabilize vehicles and lower visibility by blowing debris or dust into the roadway.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Only when changing lanes.
note: Frequently check mirrors so you remain aware of the positions and speeds of vehicles around you rather than staring ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop and inch forward until you can see clearly both ways.,b:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.,c:Maintain speed and rely on other drivers to stop.,d:Sound your horn and proceed quickly.
note: If you can’t see cross traffic, stop and creep forward until you have a clear view before proceeding.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the roadway but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane without checking.
note: Animals near the road may move unpredictably or be followed by others; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Set the parking brake.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: Scan mirrors to be aware of traffic behind you as you ease off the accelerator and apply the brake for a smooth stop.

question: To improve visibility in heavy rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: Use low beams in precipitation and fog; high beams reflect and reduce visibility.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop whether or not children are present.,c:Always sound your horn as you pass children.
note: School crossing signs warn you to be alert and prepared to stop for children who may enter the roadway.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane when it is safe.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the wheel, keep control, lift off the accelerator, slow gradually, and exit the traffic lane when safe; lightly apply brakes if needed.

question: Which action helps prevent you from becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the driver in front of you.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit.,c:Relax and concentrate on driving.,d:Honk repeatedly at slow drivers.
note: Avoid aggressive driving by staying calm, concentrating on driving, following speed limits, and not taking other drivers' actions personally.

question: Under foggy, low-visibility conditions you should:
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed to get out of the fog quickly.
note: In fog, use low beams and reduce speed; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road in a safe location.

question: Which of the following is considered a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.,d:Only use of electronic devices.
note: A distraction is any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving and can lead to crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection marked with a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always come to a complete stop whether traffic is present or not.
note: A yield sign requires you to give the right-of-way to traffic close enough to cause a conflict; stop if necessary.

question: If you are driving alongside another vehicle in a multi-lane road, you should:
options: a:Move ahead or drop back so you are not beside the other vehicle.,b:Maintain your speed and stay alongside them.,c:Ask the other driver to slow down.
note: Avoid driving beside another vehicle where you may be in its blind spot; either pull ahead or fall behind to reduce risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds regardless of distance.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:As soon as you are past the bumper.
note: You may move back when the passed vehicle’s headlights (or front) are visible in your rearview mirror and it’s safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge when clear.,b:Stop and wait for a big gap before entering.,c:Reduce speed to 25 mph before entering the lane.
note: Accelerate on the ramp to match highway speeds and merge smoothly when a safe gap appears; do not stop on the ramp.

question: Which of the following is the correct way to use your feet when driving?
options: a:Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake.,b:Use your left foot for braking.,c:Always brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: Use your right foot for both accelerating and braking and apply the brake smoothly with increasing pressure to stop safely.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Knowledge only.,c:Right-of-way privileges.,d:License status immediately.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment and coordination needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of driving.,d:Keeping a steady speed.
note: Slowing to stare at collisions or unusual events causes congestion and delays.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while a traffic signal shows green, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer's directions.,b:Obey the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Follow what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: Officers' directions override traffic signals and signs; follow an officer's orders for safety and legal compliance.

question: When a school bus ahead stops to load or unload children with red lights flashing and the stop arm out, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.,c:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.
note: Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm; remain stopped until the bus resumes motion and signals are withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should be sure:
options: a:You can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:You look over your shoulder only.
note: You should only return to the driving lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through the water.,b:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,c:Slam on the brakes before entering the water.
note: Never drive through flooded areas; even shallow water can hide hazards or sweep your vehicle away—seek an alternate route.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and go only when the way is clear.

question: On a multilane road where there is a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does it mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted only by traffic next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When dashed and solid yellow lines are paired, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross to pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.

question: When an approaching car has very bright headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look below their headlights.
note: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, do not stare directly at them. Look toward the right edge of your lane until the oncoming vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrians have finished crossing.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Pull to the right and pass them.,d:Speed up to get ahead of them.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they clear the roadway.

question: In a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,c:Refuse to move your vehicle for any reason.,d:Block the lane to prevent others from passing.
note: If safe and possible, remove the vehicle from the travel lane to avoid blocking traffic after a minor crash.

question: Pavement is especially treacherous and slippery:
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:When it is clean and dry.
note: Roadways are most slippery during the first half hour of rain because oils and residues mix with the water.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, you should:
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot.,b:Signal only and then change lanes.,c:Check mirrors only, no need to signal if it's quick.
note: Always signal first, then check mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear before moving laterally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park uphill where there is a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If the road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:
options: a:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,b:The same as normal.,c:Closer than normal.,d:Two feet shorter than usual.
note: Slippery roads require extra stopping distance; increase following space accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow center lines to pass another vehicle when:
options: a:The yellow line next to your lane is broken.,b:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,c:The yellow line next to the opposite lane is broken.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means passing is allowed from your side when it is safe.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn fully and look out the back window.,c:Only check blind spots.,d:Ignore rear traffic unless merging.
note: Regularly checking your rearview mirror helps you anticipate changing traffic conditions behind you.

question: Before driving, remove all snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:All windows and mirrors.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.,d:Only the hood and roof.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before setting out.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you turn on to be seen?
options: a:On your headlights.,b:On your parking lights.,c:Up the instrument panel lights.,d:On your hazard lights.
note: Use headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles or when others may have difficulty seeing you; use low beams if wipers are needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers who are turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight or with the right-of-way.,b:No one; the turning driver always has the right-of-way.,c:Overtaking cars only.
note: A left-turning driver must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or otherwise has the right-of-way before completing the turn.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.,d:Only at marked crosswalks.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times, whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

question: Allow extra following space when you are behind a:
options: a:Motorcycle.,b:Station wagon.,c:Passenger vehicle.,d:Convertible.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are harder to see; give extra space to react if they brake or fall.

question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The same as a yield sign.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: Treat a flashing red light as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when the way is clear.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, possessing or consuming open containers of alcohol is:
options: a:Illegal.,b:Legal if you are not driving.,c:Legal if the driver is not intoxicated.,d:Allowed for passengers only.
note: It is illegal for occupants to possess or drink from open containers of alcohol in a vehicle while it is being operated.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, you should:
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking until traction returns.,b:Shift into a lower gear immediately to slow down.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to restore traction.
note: When tires lose contact you should gently reduce speed by easing off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until you regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, how do you check your blind spot?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely solely on the side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, you must look over your shoulder to see areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,d:Sound your horn and pass quickly.
note: You must not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:You have passed the vehicle's front bumper.
note: Return to the right lane only after you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Check behind you and then watch the vehicle ahead before moving.,b:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,c:Speed up and expect other drivers to make room.
note: Always check for traffic to the sides and behind your vehicle before merging into a gap in highway traffic.

question: What do broken yellow center lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and allow passing when safe.,b:They indicate no passing zones.,c:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean passing is permitted from the side next to the broken line when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route; do not back up.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Stop on the ramp and wait for a gap to return.
note: Do not back up on the freeway or shoulder; drive to the next exit and circle back safely to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Slowly pass stopped vehicles without stopping.,c:Stop, listen, and then proceed without looking.
note: At locations where people or other traffic may cross, scan left and right to ensure nothing is approaching before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if you and a driver on your left arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right goes first.

question: What is the only medically proven method to lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to process the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Get fresh air or take a cold shower.
note: Nothing speeds up alcohol elimination; only the passage of time reduces BAC and alcohol's impairing effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection you should:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Assume oncoming traffic must yield to you.,c:Never yield; complete the turn quickly.,d:Only yield to vehicles, not pedestrians.
note: Left turns require yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until it is safe to turn.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Park with all four wheels off the traveled roadway if possible.,b:Stop in the right lane.,c:Leave the vehicle where it stopped.,d:Turn off your emergency flashers immediately.
note: If possible, move completely off the main traveled portion of the road and stop there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle when:
options: a:You can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:You have passed the vehicle's front bumper.,c:You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: You may return when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe distance.

question: Collisions become more likely when:
options: a:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,b:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,c:One lane travels slightly faster than the other lanes consistently.
note: Driving at speeds that differ substantially from surrounding traffic increases the chance of collisions.

question: If you are prescribed a medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Have someone follow you home.,b:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,c:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about its effects on driving.,d:Avoid taking any medications.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Check with your doctor or pharmacist about any effect on driving ability.

question: When exiting the freeway on a downhill curved ramp you should:
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Slow only after you enter the curve.,c:Reduce speed to the freeway posted limit.,d:Stop at the start of the ramp.
note: Reduce speed before entering the curve; braking while in a curve may cause a skid.

question: When should you reduce speed when approaching a curve?
options: a:Before entering the curve.,b:Only if you feel like it.,c:When you are halfway through the curve.,d:After you are in the curve.
note: Slow down before the curve so you don’t have to brake while turning, which can cause a skid.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed so:
options: a:The truck has room to stop safely.,b:Other drivers can merge onto the freeway.,c:Other drivers can slow down without consequence.
note: Because large trucks need longer stopping distances than cars, other drivers should avoid cutting closely in front of them.

question: In rainy weather, when are you most likely to skid while turning or stopping?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:One half hour after it stops raining.
note: During the first half hour of rain, oil and residue on the pavement combine with water and can make the road especially slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning left at a red light after a complete stop is allowed only when:
options: a:You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it.,b:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After stopping, a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street unless a sign prohibits it; yield to other traffic and pedestrians.

question: Adjust the driver's seat so you can see the pavement how far in front of your vehicle?
options: a:12 to 15 feet.,b:5 to 10 feet.,c:12 to 15 inches.
note: Set the seat to allow a view of the pavement about 12 to 15 feet ahead and position your chest about 10 to 12 inches from the steering column for control and visibility.

question: You are following a motorcycle and want to pass. What should you do?
options: a:Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Remain in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.,c:Sound your horn to force the motorcycle onto the shoulder.
note: Treat motorcycles as vehicles that occupy a full lane; move fully into the left lane to pass safely and never crowd a motorcycle by sharing its lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight and to pedestrians with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right, the best action is to:
options: a:Change lanes to the left when it is safe.,b:Slow down in the right lane.,c:Maintain your speed and position in the right lane.
note: When traffic permits, move to the left lane to allow merging vehicles room to enter from on-ramps on your right.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Whenever asked after a traffic stop or after a collision.,b:Only if you are involved in a collision.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: Kentucky drivers must carry proof of financial responsibility (insurance) and present it to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

question: When poor weather reduces visibility, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead so you have more time to react to hazards you may not see right away.

question: Only which of the following can reduce blood alcohol concentration and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Time.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Eating fatty foods.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and lower BAC; food or coffee do not speed this process.

question: How often is it recommended you glance at your speedometer while driving?
options: a:Once a minute.,b:Once every ten minutes.,c:Twice a minute.,d:Continuously.
note: Glance at your speedometer about once a minute to help maintain a safe and legal speed; make it a regular habit.

question: When a large truck ahead begins a right turn onto a street with two lanes in each direction, the truck:
options: a:May need to swing wide to the left before completing the right turn.,b:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,c:May complete the turn in either lane without adjusting.
note: Long trucks often swing wide when turning so their rear wheels can follow the correct path; give them extra room.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent will:
options: a:Nearly double your chances of being in an accident.,b:Have no effect on your driving.,c:Never put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a BAC of 0.02 percent increases crash risk significantly; each 0.02 percent increment raises the chance of a fatal crash.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Wait — allow time for your body to metabolize it.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only method that lowers blood alcohol concentration; other measures do not speed elimination.

question: Which factor listed affects how a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:The person's weight.,b:The person's intelligence.,c:The person's height.
note: A person's weight, sex, food in the stomach, and number of drinks consumed affect alcohol absorption and BAC.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should keep your headlights set to:
options: a:Low beam.,b:High beam until within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:High beam at all times.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver ahead; use high beams only when no vehicles are nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires that drivers:
options: a:Be constantly alert and be able to safely drive at higher speeds.,b:Only be able to drive at increased speeds.,c:Drive the same as on surface streets.
note: Safe interstate driving requires both constant alertness and the ability to operate safely at the higher speeds of highway traffic.

question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down significantly before moving.
note: Always check mirrors and blind spots by glancing over your shoulder to ensure a lane change is safe.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to clear the tracks.,b:The crossing is in a city or town.,c:You are transporting two or more young children only.,d:The train signals are silent.
note: Never stop on the tracks; ensure there is room to fully clear them before proceeding.

question: What may happen if you take prescription medication while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It will have no effect.
note: Many legal medications interact with alcohol and may impair driving ability or dangerously increase side effects.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop and may not stop in time.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.,c:Because large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Due to their size and weight, large vehicles require greater stopping distances; sudden stops in front of them increase collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Signal before changing lanes.
note: Never change lanes while you are inside an intersection. Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder for blind spots.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating other vehicles and failing to watch for workers and equipment.,b:Driving below the posted speed.,c:Using turn signals.
note: Following too closely and not watching for workers or equipment are both dangerous in work zones and increase crash risk.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What is the first action you should take?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal to increase space.,b:Sound your horn and brake hard.,c:Swerve into the adjacent lane immediately.
note: Removing your foot from the accelerator creates space without the need to brake abruptly or swerve, helping avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a left turn at an upcoming corner, you must yield to:
options: a:Pedestrians and any vehicles that have the right-of-way.,b:Only vehicles approaching from the right.,c:Only oncoming vehicles also turning left.
note: When turning left yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and oncoming traffic that has the right-of-way or a green signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Avoid driving alongside it for long stretches.,b:Follow it closely to reduce wind drag.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,d:Pass only on the right.
note: Large vehicles have big blind spots—avoid lingering beside them where the driver can't see you.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected and proceed with caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often have unusual conditions; slow down, watch for workers and equipment, and follow posted directions.

question: If you suffer a sudden tire blowout, you should:
options: a:Use the brakes lightly and gradually slow down.,b:Pump the brakes quickly.,c:Apply the brakes fully and immediately.
note: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly, stay straight, ease off the gas, and use the brakes gently to slow down.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Alertness only.,c:Coordination only.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration—skills needed for safe driving.

question: To help prevent skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Speed up going into curves and slow to exit them.,c:Shift into a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
note: Reduce speed before curves and intersections; braking on a curve can cause a loss of traction and a skid.

question: At night you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: Increase following distance at night for extra reaction time, and use proper headlight settings to avoid glare.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, they may:
options: a:Use the left lane as needed to make the turn.,b:Cut through all lanes of traffic.,c:Only wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane when preparing to make a left turn; expect them to behave like other vehicles in such situations.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.,b:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.,d:Mirrors fully remove blind spots.
note: Even with mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have much larger blind spots than typical cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; entering and blocking cross traffic is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not enter an intersection if doing so will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Even with a green signal, do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it before the light turns red to avoid blocking traffic.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving distracting?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the call cost.,c:It draws the attention of other drivers.,d:It reduces engine performance.
note: Cell phone use occupies hands, eyes, and attention, increasing crash risk even for skilled drivers.

question: Tailgating (following too closely) often:
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and lead to aggressive behavior.,b:Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,c:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,d:Is the best way to signal impatience.
note: Driving too close is dangerous, provokes other drivers, and can result in legal penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multi-lane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should begin the turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it's safe.,c:The center lane of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far-left lane and turn into the nearest left lane.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines mean:
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the left only.,c:Passing is permitted from the right only.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is prohibited in both directions.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy weather, you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Move onto the shoulder as soon as it begins to rain.
note: Lowering speed reduces the chance your tires will ride up on standing water and lose contact with the pavement.

question: In bad weather, you should:
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Drive in a lower gear at all times.,d:Brake hard to reduce speed quickly.
note: Smooth steering and braking reduce loss of traction and enhance vehicle control in adverse conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (right).,b:Away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep them pointed straight ahead.
note: When parked uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway so the car will roll off the road if it moves.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulder.,b:Trust the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the outside mirror.,d:Use parking sensors only.
note: Blind spots are not visible through mirrors; glance over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Expect them to yield to you.,c:Honk to let them know you are there.,d:Speed up to clear the crosswalk.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians with canes or guide dogs must be given the right-of-way.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance to allow extra reaction time.,b:Decrease your following distance because motorcycles stop quickly.,c:Pass immediately to avoid being behind them.
note: Motorcycles can stop or maneuver more quickly; leave extra space so you can react safely to sudden moves.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) safety belt system, you should:
options: a:Wear both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: When available, use both lap and shoulder belts; using only one part greatly reduces protection.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction due to water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.,b:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to stop the sliding.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, gently reduce speed by easing off the gas and avoid braking until traction returns to the tires.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed through the intersection without stopping.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; prepare to stop if you have not already entered the intersection.

question: Which best defines distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,d:Anything that improves driving performance.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that diverts your eyes, hands, or mind from driving and is a leading contributor to crashes.

question: Roads and highways are most slippery when:
options: a:It has just begun to rain.,b:It has been raining heavily for several hours.,c:They are clean and dry.
note: Road surfaces become very slippery shortly after rain starts because oils and residues mix with the water.

question: There is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. You should:
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,b:Slow down and pass carefully.,c:Make eye contact then pass in front of them.,d:Speed up to pass before they cross.
note: Even without marked crosswalks, you must yield and allow pedestrians to finish crossing safely.

question: Your car may begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:35 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start around 35 mph when tires can no longer channel water away and lose contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers entering interstate traffic from an acceleration ramp do?
options: a:Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:May force their way into traffic.,d:Come to a full stop at the end of the ramp before entering.
note: When merging from an acceleration lane onto the interstate, yield to traffic already on the highway and merge safely when there is a gap.

question: A good driver should:
options: a:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Stare directly ahead all the time.
note: To drive safely, continuously scan the area around your vehicle so you know what other road users are doing.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Keep cruise control on.
note: Tires have less traction on wet or icy roads; slow down and drive more cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but can't find a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to make room.,d:Back up on the ramp to get a better view.
note: If no gap exists, slow on the ramp to wait for a space so you can accelerate to freeway speed before merging.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment and reduce your speed.,b:Change lanes and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up because the lane ends ahead.
note: Construction areas often have changed lanes and workers; slow down and follow signs and directions for safety.

question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,b:Loudly play the radio while driving to distract yourself.,c:Drive on the interstate to release stress.,d:Drive faster to get over the anger quickly.
note: Emotions impair driving ability; calm down before operating a vehicle to avoid dangerous mistakes.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,b:If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC means driving is not impaired.,d:Alcohol only affects inexperienced drivers.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment essential to safe driving; even below the legal limit it can reduce ability to drive safely.

question: When a centerline is marked with a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line, passing is:
options: a:Allowed only from the side beside the broken yellow line.,b:Allowed from either side at any time.,c:Prohibited from both directions.
note: A broken yellow next to a solid means the side with the broken line may pass when safe; the side with the solid line may not.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, you should steer:
options: a:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
note: When facing oncoming traffic on one side and parked cars on the other, aim for the middle of the available lane to maximize clearance on both sides.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally (not in a crosswalk), you must:
options: a:Stop and yield to them.,b:Honk to force them to move.,c:Proceed because they are violating the law.,d:Flash your lights and continue.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians anytime they are in danger of being struck, even if out of a crosswalk.

question: A school bus stopped in your lane with red lights flashing means you should:
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think the children have exited the bus.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus uses flashing red lights, motorists in the same lane must stop and stay stopped until the lights are turned off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking an intersection while you face a green light, what should you do?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection until you can completely clear it.,b:Partially enter to establish right-of-way.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,d:Honk and push through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across to avoid blocking it and potential citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice when driving on an interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,c:Proceeding to the next exit if you miss yours.
note: Always signal lane changes; failing to signal is unsafe and illegal. Slow traffic should use the right lanes, and missed exits should be taken at the next exit.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, you should turn your wheels:
options: a:Toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Away from the curb.,c:Keep them straight.
note: When parking downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: When traveling through a work zone you should:
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,c:Pass as soon as you get a chance.
note: Increase your following distance and reduce speed in work zones to protect workers and allow for sudden stops.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One.,b:Two.,c:Three.,d:None; alcohol has no effect.
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair driving. Even a single drink can affect your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
