note: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to others, and go only when the way is clear.

question: When parking next to a curb, when must you use your turn signals?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
note: Drivers must signal whenever pulling toward a curb or pulling away from it so other road users understand your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a vehicle entering your interstate lane from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Change lanes if possible to allow them room to merge.,b:Speed up to pass them before they merge.,c:Ignore them since you have the right-of-way.
note: When safe, move over to let entering vehicles merge smoothly; cooperative driving reduces crash risk.

question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes the turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn ahead of the truck or bus.,c:Squeeze between it and the curb.,d:Honk to make it stop turning.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to turn; do not try to cut between them and the curb or you risk a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you make a left turn when on a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: On a one-way street you make a left turn from the lane closest to the left curb into the nearest legal lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When overtaking another vehicle going the same direction, you should:
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible before returning to the lane.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass as slowly as possible to avoid surprises.
note: Complete the pass promptly and safely, then return to your driving lane only when you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

question: What message is shown on a red, octagon-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:Stop.,b:Do not enter.,c:One-way.
note: An octagonal red sign always means STOP; you must come to a complete stop and yield to those with the right-of-way.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Locks the front wheels and causes a loss of steering.,b:Helps you stop faster.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.,d:Prevents skidding entirely.
note: Hard braking on slick surfaces can lock brakes and cause you to lose steering control.

question: Reaction time is slower after:
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.,d:Exercising.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, reduces vision, and decreases alertness.

question: If a child is bicycling near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden movements.,b:Beep your horn to warn them.,c:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; slow down and be prepared for sudden direction changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: A double solid yellow centerline indicates traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not permitted from either side.

question: Under normal conditions, maintain a following distance of at least:
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.,d:Five seconds.
note: Under normal weather, road, and traffic conditions a minimum three-second following distance is recommended.

question: Which area is most likely to become icy after snow or rain in cold weather?
options: a:A road in a shaded area.,b:A residential road.,c:A hilly, open road.
note: Shaded portions of a roadway freeze sooner and thaw later than exposed sections, making them more likely to be icy.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can do what to your driving?
options: a:Impair your judgment.,b:Help you be a better driver.,c:Make you feel better.,d:Improve concentration.
note: Lack of sleep slows reaction time, decreases awareness, and impairs judgment similar to alcohol or drugs.

question: What should you do when driving through a highway construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Pass the construction zone carefully and avoid 'rubbernecking'.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Drive faster than the posted limit to clear the zone quickly.
note: Do not slow down to stare at incidents or workers ('rubberneck'); travel through construction zones carefully and obey posted instructions.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.,b:Drive more slowly directly behind the motorcycle.,c:Be ready to use your horn frequently.
note: Give motorcycles at least a three- to four-second following distance because they can stop quickly and are more vulnerable.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed from both directions.,c:Allowed only from your direction.,d:Allowed only for turning vehicles.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit crossing the centerline to pass in either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict, slowing or stopping if necessary.,b:Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: A yield sign means slow down or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow quick stopping.,c:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require much more distance to stop than passenger cars, especially at higher speeds.

question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard while turning.
note: Slow to a safe speed before a curve; avoid heavy braking while turning to maintain stability.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, you should:
options: a:Steer to the left to regain control.,b:Steer to the right immediately.,c:Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: When the rear skids left, steer in the direction of the skid so the front and rear of the vehicle realign; avoid heavy braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check blind spots before changing lanes, a driver should:
options: a:Turn their head and look over the appropriate shoulder.,b:Rely only on the outside mirrors.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show all areas beside your vehicle; look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: Before you back up, you should:
options: a:Check behind the vehicle before getting in.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.,d:Roll down all windows but not look back.
note: Inspect the area behind the vehicle before entering; small children or objects may be hard to see from the seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking an intersection is illegal even if the signal is green.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Slow to 10 mph and proceed with caution.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Stop only if children are visible.
note: You must stop when bus red lights and stop arm are activated and wait until the signals stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on interstate highways in Kentucky?
options: a:65 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:75 mph.,d:45 mph.
note: The default interstate speed limit is 65 mph unless signs indicate a different limit.

question: You can help the driver behind you keep a safe distance by:
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling well in advance helps following drivers keep a safe gap.

question: If you become tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop and get rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink something with caffeine and keep going.
note: To avoid fatigue-related crashes, stop and rest or switch drivers; caffeine or fresh air do not replace sleep.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Always signal before changing lanes or turning.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Use your horn frequently to assert your right-of-way.
note: Clear signaling and courteous driving reduce the chance of misunderstandings and aggressive reactions from others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an all-way stop, you should yield the right-of-way to any driver who:
options: a:Arrived before you.,b:Is on your left.,c:Is signaling to make a turn.
note: Vehicles proceed through an all-way stop in the order they arrived; yield to drivers who arrived before you.

question: On a freeway you should look farther ahead than on a city street in order to:
options: a:See potential hazards earlier.,b:Keep up with cars behind you.,c:Reduce the need to check mirrors.,d:Ignore merging traffic.
note: Looking farther ahead on high-speed roads helps you detect hazards and changes earlier.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What important step should you take when preparing to turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Always move to the left lane first.,c:Increase your speed before turning.,d:Signal only after starting the turn.
note: Before turning, look left, right, and behind to ensure it’s safe and adjust speed accordingly.

question: Alcohol in any concentration acts as:
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:Neither a depressant nor stimulant.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and reduces the ability to concentrate and stay alert.

question: Blue traffic signs primarily provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas, hospitals, or food.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage and distance to destinations.
note: Blue signs are service signs that direct drivers to facilities and services like hospitals, gas, and rest areas.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right.,c:Not turn the steering wheel at all.
note: Steer in the direction of the skid (left, in this case) to help the front of the vehicle realign with the rear; avoid sudden braking.

question: To reduce glare from the headlights of an oncoming vehicle, you should:
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stare at the centerline for the whole time.,c:Flash your high beams at the other vehicle.
note: Look toward the right edge of the roadway briefly to avoid being blinded, then continue checking the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, you must:
options: a:Come to a full stop and treat the intersection as an all-way stop.,b:Proceed if the intersection appears clear.,c:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.,d:Follow traffic flow without stopping.
note: Non-operational signals require drivers to stop and yield as though at an all-way stop unless directed otherwise.

question: Driving while under the influence of medication that impairs you is:
options: a:Illegal under all circumstances.,b:Allowed if the medication is prescribed.,c:Allowed if you do not feel drowsy.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your ability to operate a vehicle safely, prescription or otherwise.

question: As you approach an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and proceed carefully after checking for hazards or cross traffic.

question: If you become tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop to rest or switch drivers.,b:Drink coffee and continue.,c:Open your windows to stay awake.,d:Turn up the music loudly.
note: Stopping to rest or changing drivers is safer than relying on temporary measures like caffeine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless a sign shows otherwise, the speed limit in a business or residential area is:
options: a:35 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:15 mph.
note: Unless posted differently, the handbook indicates a default speed limit of 35 mph in business and residential areas; always obey posted limits.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean for drivers on your side of the road?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:You may pass on the right only.,d:You must turn left only when clear.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may cross the centerline to pass when it’s safe and no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:
options: a:Using side mirrors and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only the rearview mirror.,c:Using only side mirrors.,d:Stopping on the ramp to check traffic.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to see real positions of vehicles before merging onto the freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should enter at:
options: a:At or near the speed of the existing freeway traffic.,b:The legal posted limit no matter traffic.,c:Much more slowly than freeway traffic.,d:Below 20 mph for safety.
note: You should merge at or near the speed of freeway traffic unless that speed exceeds the law.

question: Drivers must obey instructions from which of these personnel at work zones?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons).,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down.,d:Pedestrians.
note: Flaggers direct traffic in work zones and their instructions must be followed for everyone's safety.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,b:Because motorcycles do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,c:Because motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles are capable of rapid stops; tailgating reduces your ability to avoid rear-end collisions if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly.

question: If everyone has exited your vehicle, is it acceptable to leave the engine running?
options: a:If you will only be away for a couple of minutes.,b:Never leave the engine running.,c:If you will be away for less than an hour.,d:If parked in a secure lot.
note: Kentucky law requires you to turn off the engine and remove the key when leaving a vehicle; always lock it even for short absences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Ease off the accelerator to help them pass safely.,b:Increase your speed to prevent them from passing.,c:Press hard on your brakes to force them to slow down.
note: Cooperating by easing up slightly helps the other driver pass safely and reduces the chance of a risky maneuver.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what is the safest response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes.,d:Steer hard immediately to the shoulder.
note: If a tire blows out, remove your foot from the accelerator and let the vehicle slow; apply brakes lightly only after the car has slowed.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:It is hard to judge distance and vehicle speed in the dark.,b:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,c:The speed limit is increased at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distances and speeds; drivers can only see as far as their headlights allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often:
options: a:Increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.,b:Saves significant travel time.,c:Helps maneuver safely around obstacles.,d:Reduces fuel consumption.
note: High speed is a leading contributing factor in serious crashes and does not meaningfully save time.

question: Which statement about driving speed is accurate?
options: a:As speed increases, the chance of a fatality rises and you should increase following distance.,b:Higher speed does not affect stopping distance.,c:As speed increases, you can decrease your following distance.
note: Faster speeds increase stopping distances and the risk of fatal crashes, so increase your following distance as speed rises.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is prohibited from either direction.
note: The broken line permits passing for the adjacent lane; the solid line forbids passing for the lane next to it.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, you should slow down and turn on:
options: a:Your headlights.,b:Your parking lights.,c:Your emergency flashers only.
note: When you cannot see other vehicles clearly, use headlights to make your vehicle visible to others and reduce speed.

question: From top to bottom, the correct order of traffic signal lights is:
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, red, yellow.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: Traffic signals are arranged vertically as red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,d:Only buses may cross for boarding.
note: Broken yellow centerlines allow passing in either direction when there’s no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: You must never go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate; wait until the gate is fully raised and it is safe to proceed.

question: If you strike a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return and then exchange information.
note: If you damage parked property and the owner is not present, leave a note with your contact information on the vehicle.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should occupants still do?
options: a:Wear seat belts.,b:Not wear seat belts.,c:Wear belts behind their backs.,d:Disable the airbags.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; lap and shoulder belts must still be used for best protection.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some over-the-counter cold medicines.,b:Cough syrups only.,c:None of the above.
note: Many legal and illegal substances—including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, and some cough and cold medicines—can impair driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' signal flashed and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before you go.,d:Flash your horn and proceed.
note: You must yield to pedestrians and give them time to finish crossing the intersection before you proceed, even on a green light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads with two-way traffic, drive in the right lane unless passing or turning left; if being passed on both sides, move right when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is prohibited:
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is retracted and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.
note: Drivers approaching a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm must stop and remain stopped until the bus signals it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to make a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,c:Approach in the right lane but move toward the middle before turning.
note: Approach the turn from the lane nearest the right curb, signal and slow to complete a safe right-hand turn without cutting corners.

question: When driving through a work zone you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to get through quickly.,c:Maintain your normal speed throughout the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be ready to stop; workers and equipment may be present near traffic lanes.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights very bright.,d:Flash your headlights frequently.
note: At night you must be able to stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights to avoid hazards.

question: Yellow centerlines on the road separate:
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Bike lanes from traffic lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road; broken or solid patterns indicate passing rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,c:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
note: If in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At speeds of 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to crash if you:
options: a:Match the general speed of other vehicles (stay within that range).,b:Drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,c:Drive much slower than surrounding traffic.,d:Constantly change lanes to pass.
note: Traveling smoothly with the flow of traffic reduces speed differentials that cause multi-vehicle crashes.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is in bad condition it can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Bad suspension affects vehicle stability and control, making it harder to steer and safely handle the car.

question: You should allow extra following distance when following:
options: a:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (e.g., large truck),b:A station wagon.,c:A small passenger car.,d:An emergency vehicle.
note: Give extra space behind large vehicles that cannot see you and that may block your view of the road ahead.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.,d:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing else will sober you up faster.

question: The best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation is to:
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle by scanning front, sides, and rear.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused only ahead of your car.
note: Constantly observing your surroundings gives you time to react to potential problems before they become critical.

question: Which statement best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They expect other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.,d:They always assume they have the right-of-way.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and position themselves to compensate and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:Traffic on the street you are entering moves to the left.,b:You increase your speed before the turn.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the right.
note: Turning left onto a one-way street is allowed only when traffic on that street flows to the left and no signs prohibit the turn.

question: To make quick steering maneuvers safely, your hands should be:
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other at the top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the wheel.,d:At the bottom of the wheel only.
note: Placing hands on opposite sides of the wheel promotes control and safe turning, especially at speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle moving in the same direction, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds have passed.,c:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: You should only return to the right lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe distance.

question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days primarily to:
options: a:Make your vehicle more visible to other drivers.,b:Keep the engine warm.,c:Warn others about poor weather.
note: If visibility is reduced or you are using windshield wipers, turn on your low-beam headlights so others can see your vehicle.

question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead when you:
options: a:Are being tailgated by another driver.,b:Are following a small passenger car.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking to reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a row of parked vehicles you should:
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.,c:Expect all pedestrians and drivers to yield to you.
note: Leave space between you and parked cars because people or vehicles can suddenly appear from between them.

question: If your vehicle starts skidding, you should:
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer to recover control.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.,c:Brake lightly and steer the opposite way of the skid.
note: Do not use the brakes during a skid; instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.

question: A flashing red light at an intersection is equivalent to:
options: a:A stop sign — you must stop and proceed when safe.,b:A yield sign.,c:A light about to turn green.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, then continue only when no vehicles or pedestrians are in the way.

question: As your speed increases, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Change lanes frequently to keep up with traffic.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Look well ahead of your vehicle to allow time to react.,d:Maintain the same following distance.
note: Stopping distance increases as speed increases. Look far ahead so you have room and time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the maximum posted speed limit only when:
options: a:Road and weather conditions are ideal.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The posted maximum speed is legal only under ideal conditions; drivers should reduce speed for rain, snow, heavy traffic, or poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot into the street, drivers should:
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.,b:Assume pedestrians will yield and only stop if they block you.,c:Stop only if a pedestrian is standing on the sidewalk.
note: You must stop before entering the sidewalk area to check for pedestrians and yield to any who are crossing.

question: After having several beers, the effects will be reduced only by:
options: a:Waiting several hours.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol; showers or coffee do not speed this process.

question: A driver's license should be considered a:
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: Driving privileges are granted by the state and can be taken away for unsafe or illegal conduct.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline you may:
options: a:Cross the line to change lanes when it is safe.,b:Remain in your lane at all times, no crossing allowed.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,d:Proceed if you are going straight.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in order of arrival.

question: How is driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic usually viewed?
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and attempt risky passes.,d:Required by law.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create hazards as other drivers may try unsafe maneuvers to pass you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Left, then right, then left again.,b:Only to the left.,c:Only to the right.
note: Look to both sides and then left again before entering because vehicles from the left will be closer due to intersection geometry.

question: Which of these statements about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are removed if you have one outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be seen by only using rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

question: When changing lanes you should never:
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or without checking your blind spot.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Do not make sudden, spontaneous lane changes; always check mirrors, signal, and check blind spots before moving.

question: At an intersection showing a flashing yellow light you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop, then enter when safe.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully after checking for hazards or cross traffic.

question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when you see children present.
note: Crossing guards' directions are law and must be followed whenever they are managing pedestrian crossings.

question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Driving at lower speeds on wet pavement reduces the risk of tires losing contact with the road and hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way and proceed.,c:Require pedestrians to wait for your vehicle.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection before pedestrians move.
note: Even on green, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; yield when turning on green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than traffic for the first 200 feet.,c:Enter as soon as the first two vehicles pass.,d:Honk and accelerate into traffic immediately.
note: Merge only when there’s a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the flow speed safely.

question: Large trucks commonly lose speed when:
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving in long, gradual curves.,c:Driving down long, gradual hills.
note: Because heavy vehicles take longer to accelerate, trucks often slow when climbing long or steep inclines; give them extra space.

question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.,d:Change lanes without signaling.
note: Glance over the shoulder to check blind spots before lane changes and signal your move.

question: At a railroad crossing with gates down and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted.,b:Drive around the lowered gates if you don't see a train.,c:Slow and crawl under the gate.,d:Signal other drivers to go around.
note: It is illegal and dangerous to drive around lowered gates; wait until lights stop and gates are up.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning in heavy rain, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive at speeds for ideal conditions.,c:Apply the brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water; reducing speed in wet conditions is the best way to avoid it.
